newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire's Mobutu, Kabila could meet on warship - paper.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu, Kabila could meet on warship - paper.

text.p: Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila could meet for first peace talks on a South African warship in international waters, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

South Africa's Business Day said the ailing Mobutu, whose authority has shrunk to the capital Kinshasa and a western third of Zaire, could come face-to-face with Kabila on the naval supply ship Outeniqua.
South African officials were not immediately available for comment on the report, which gave no source for its information.
Meeting on a ship, possibly off the coast of Zaire itself or off the neighbouring Angolan enclave of Cabinda, would allow the cancer-stricken Mobutu to hold talks close to Zaire, the paper said.

Kabila's rebels, battling to end Mobutu's reign, have captured most of the gigantic and impoverished Central African country in a rebellion that began in October. They control all main cities apart from Kinshasa, which is their ultimate aim.
Kabila has said he will only meet Mobutu to discuss how he will stand down as Zaire's leader after 32 years in power.
